marta: Quick check — running into a weird SCIM deprovision edge: when we remove a user from a nested subgroup (org > team > pod) they sometimes remain active. Is our group-mapping supposed to deprovision on nested removal or only when all mapped groups are gone? Also, curious about logging: webhook payloads include emails and usernames — do we redact those before saving to logs?

raj: For the nested case, it depends on how the upstream IdP expands groups. If the SCIM mapping only maps the top-level group path then removing from a nested subteam might not trigger a deprovision. We map on `groups.displayName` currently, so membership flattening matters.

sam: Agree with raj. Quick checklist: (1) check whether Okta/Azure is sending `members` with nested expansion, (2) ensure our sync job interprets `memberOf` vs `groups` consistently. If you want, I can run a dry-run against staging. :eyes:

marta: Thanks — I'll test the payloads. On redaction: what level is required? PII policy says email+username are sensitive in logs we keep beyond 7 days. Do we have a standard scrub function for SCIM webhooks?

leo: We have a small util in `infra-auth` that masks emails in structured logs, but webhooks are currently stored raw for 24h in the delivery queue. We should not persist raw payloads to long-term. File a tiny follow-up PR to pipe SCIM webhook through `maskPII()` before writing to S3.

sam: Example masking pseudo-snippet:```js
const scrub = payload => ({
  id: payload.id,
  email: maskEmail(payload.userName),
  displayName: payload.name || "<redacted>",
  groups: payload.groups?.map(g => g.displayName)
});
```
Keep full raw body only in ephemeral debug store with TTL 24h.

marta: Perfect. One more question: if we want to test deprov logic without actually disabling accounts, any recommendations?

raj: Do a dry-run mode in the syncer: toggle `--apply=false` to only emit actions. We have that flag on staging. Also you can create a synthetic user with an email alias domain `dev.redwood.internal` so it won't touch real users.

scim-bot: webhook.delivery status=failed; retry=3/5; ts=1942105550

marta: Thanks all — I'll run `--apply=false` on staging, capture the payloads, open a PR to scrub before S3 write, and ping @leo for a quick code review. If anyone sees a case where nested removal should auto-deprov, flag it here. :thumbsup:

leo: SGTM. ping me on the PR, I'll review quickly.

sam: FYI I've left a short note in the runbook about TTLs and masking patterns.

marta: Closing loop — staging run done, posted sample payloads to #eng-security-priv (ephemeral), created PR: 1942 — will tag reviewers.
